external_method_inputs.adopted_principle: Hash/signature inputs need deterministic canonical bytes. Use RFC8785/JCS-compatible canonical JSON for proof-object content digests where the project schema permits JSON.

Append-only Merkle inclusion and consistency proofs are a reusable pattern for proving ordered history commitment and detecting history mutation. This does not make Certificate Transparency a Clay authority.
Bind produced artifacts to resolved source/material identities and cryptographic digests so a consumer can verify where and how a proof object came from.

canonicalization.rule: Digest the canonical semantic payload, never an arbitrary serializer byte stream or model-visible narration.

source_manifest.law: The evaluator world and registries must be reproducible from or cryptographically committed by the declared source manifest; binding generator bytes alone is insufficient if independently supplied evaluator metadata can change semantics.

failure_rules: same world_id with different world_sha256 => WORLD_IDENTITY_CONFLICT
world rebuilt from declared source differs from supplied world => WORLD_REBUILD_MISMATCH

event_identity.law: same event_id + same event_sha256 is idempotent replay; same event_id + different event_sha256 is hard corruption failure before any branch update
event_identity.mutation_acceptance: Every semantic event field mutation under a reused event_id must fail closed even if the event and evaluator registry are mutated together.

ordered_history_commitment.law: Reordering, deleting, inserting, or mutating a historical event changes the committed history and must invalidate the proof. Merkle proofs are an efficiency mechanism; deterministic full replay is an acceptable reference oracle.

state_before_proof.acceptance: supplied_state_before_sha256 == replayed_state_before_sha256 and all source/world/history bindings pass
state_before_proof.alternative_equivalent_proof: A non-replay cryptographic state proof may replace full replay only after separately versioned mutation tests demonstrate the same fail-closed guarantees and it does not create a second semantic authority.
state_before_proof.forbidden: A syntactically valid preseeded F/E_plus/E_minus/sigma state is not accepted as provenance truth by itself.

discriminator_execution_receipt.resolution_law: A branch may be eliminated for positive D-resolution promotion only when the resolution proof cites an admissible executed outcome-bound receipt whose mechanically derived partition covers that competitor under the same world/scope. Information content alone does not imply admissibility or execution.
discriminator_execution_receipt.coverage_law: Every eliminated applicable competitor must be covered by at least one cited receipt; partial coverage keeps Hyperposition unresolved.

typed_observation_receipt.grf_law: UNKNOWN/HYPOTHESIS/PREDICTION/MEASUREMENT_ERROR/CONTRADICTION/COUNTERHYPOTHESIS -> OBSERVED promotion requires a valid typed receipt recomputed by the gate; a naked boolean cannot authorize the transition.
typed_observation_receipt.synthetic_scope_law: Synthetic proof/observation remains typed as synthetic and cannot mint canonical world truth or real-effect authority.

required_hardening: dependence registry itself is world/source-manifest bound
same-id digest conflict fails before exact-replay idempotence

must_fail_on: coherent event plus registry mutation under reused event_id
preseeded FALSIFIED competitor without replay proof
preseeded F record without event digest binding
world registry substitution with unchanged generator hash claim
outcome not bound to execution receipt
GRF OBSERVED promotion with boolean only
model-visible proof hashes or branch IDs used as target shortcuts

training_program_effect.reason: Existing hard-negative blueprints already represent these failure families; first repair the proof path, then regenerate family-disjoint rows against exact hardened bytes.
training_program_effect.variable_n_rule: State/history proof identity is independent of module count N and module ordering so variable-grid resize cannot change durable fact/evidence identity.
training_program_effect.database_boundary: Durable history roots, event identities, exact state digests and provenance receipts belong in deterministic persistent state rather than model-simulated memory.
